newsitem.title: GERMANY: IVG plans to raise 96 dividend to 1.5 mark.
newsitem.headline: IVG plans to raise 96 dividend to 1.5 mark.

text.p: Germany's IVG Holding AG said on Friday it made a 1996 net profit of 51.2 million marks and planned to raise its 1996 dividend payment to 1.50 marks on five-mark shares.
IVG said that after allocations to reserves, the 1996 profit was 41 million marks.
It said the higher dividend payment was possible despite significant losses from the disposal of its MWB Elektronik unit in Bremerhaven and further costs arising from company restructuring.
In 1995, IVG paid a dividend of 14 marks for every 50-mark share, equivalent to 1.4 marks per five-mark share.

New shares, arising from a capital increase in November 1996, will receive a dividend payment of 38 pfennigs. The company said these shares were entitled to one quarter of the year's dividend payment.
"For 1997, we expect continued positive business developments," IVG said in a statement.
It said more details would be published at a news conference on April 16 in Duesseldorf.
